cues.zh: 未来的飞行不该再依赖螺旋桨和涡轮
cues.en: The future of flight shouldn't be things with propellers and turbines and should

cues.zh: 而应更像《星际迷航》里的场景：散发着蓝光
cues.en: be more like what you see in Star Trek; with a kind of blue glow and something

cues.zh: 并在空中无声地滑翔。
cues.en: that silently glides through the air.

cues.zh: 当我拿到大学的教职时
cues.en: When I got an appointment at University

cues.zh: 我想，现在终于有机会去探索这个了
cues.en: I thought well, now I've got the opportunity to explore this

cues.zh: 于是开始寻找能实现这一目标的物理机制。
cues.en: and started looking for physics that enabled that to happen.

cues.zh: 我发现可行的机制是电离空气
cues.en: The sort of mechanism that I found that works was ionising air

cues.zh: 然后利用电场来加速空气。
cues.en: and then using electric fields to accelerate the air.

cues.zh: 我们做到的，是有史以来第一次
cues.en: What we achieved, was the first ever sustained flight of an aeroplane

cues.zh: 由电空气动力学推进的飞机持续飞行。
cues.en: that is propelled by electroaerodynamic propulsion.

cues.zh: 从很多定义来看，这也是有史以来第一次“固态飞行”
cues.en: And that's also by many definitions the first ever solid-state flight,

cues.zh: 意思是它没有任何活动部件。
cues.en: meaning no moving parts.

cues.zh: 这个想法其实……至少可以追溯到 20 世纪 20 年代。
cues.en: Well the idea is - is kind of - it dates back until at least the 1920s.

cues.zh: 当时一位古怪的发明家开始用高压电极做实验。
cues.en: Where an eccentric inventor at the time started experimenting with high high voltage electrodes.

cues.zh: 他以为自己发现了反重力，当然事实并非如此。
cues.en: And thought he had discovered anti-gravity, which of course was not the case.

cues.zh: 但这为相关机制奠定了一些最初的基础，
cues.en: But that set some of the initial groundwork on mechanisms for creating

cues.zh: 即在大气中产生所谓的“离子风”——通过高压电极
cues.en: what's called an ionic wind in the atmosphere, by having high-voltage

cues.zh: 电离空气，进而加速这些被电离的空气。
cues.en: electrodes ionising air and then accelerating the ionised air.

cues.zh: 因此我们在做这个设计时，
cues.en: So what we did for this design is to

cues.zh: 尽量让它看起来大致像一架传统的飞机。
cues.en: try and stick to something that looks somewhat like a conventional aircraft.

cues.zh: 但在机翼下方，它没有采用传统发动机，
cues.en: But under the wing rather than conventional engines

cues.zh: 而是装有一组电极。其中包括前方的一排极细电线，
cues.en: it has a series of electrodes. And those consist of an array of very thin wires at the front,

cues.zh: 以及后方的一排翼型电极。
cues.en: and then an array of aerofoils at the back.

cues.zh: 前方那些细电线带有极高的电压——正 20,000 伏，
cues.en: Now those thin wires at the front are set at a very high voltage - plus 20,000 volts

cues.zh: 这构成了离子的来源——也就是来自大气中被电离的氮气。
cues.en: and that constitutes the source of ions - this is ionised nitrogen from the atmosphere.

cues.zh: 后面那些机翼则设置为负两万伏
cues.en: Now the the aerofoils at the back there set at minus 20,000 volts

cues.zh: 从而形成一个电场。
cues.en: and so that creates an electric field.

cues.zh: 于是离子从正极流向负极
cues.en: So the ions go from the positive to the negative

cues.zh: 一路上与中性空气分子碰撞
cues.en: colliding all the way with neutral air molecules

cues.zh: 在飞机后方形成这股气流。
cues.en: and creating this wind that goes behind the plane.

cues.zh: 这基本上就是它的飞行原理。
cues.en: And that's essentially how it flies.

cues.zh: 那次飞行大约六十米长，大概十秒钟——所以相当短。
cues.en: The flight was about sixty meters long, something like ten seconds - so quite short.

cues.zh: 这受限于我们找到的那间体育馆的尺寸。
cues.en: It was constrained by the size of the gym that we found to fly it in.

cues.zh: 由于没有无限的资金和时间，只想尽快把事情做出来
cues.en: Lacking infinite money in time and just wanting to do things as quickly as possible

cues.zh: 那就只能用手头现成的东西
cues.en: that was what was on hand

cues.zh: 于是我们就去问设施管理员能不能让我们用体育馆，
cues.en: and so we just asked the facilities manager if they would let us use the gym,

cues.zh: 他们要求我们制定一份非常长且详细的安全管理方案
cues.en: they forced us to create a very long and detailed safety management plan

cues.zh: 但之后我们就得以继续进行了。
cues.en: but then we were able to go ahead.

cues.zh: 很多次尝试都因为各种问题失败了
cues.en: Many attempts failed because of various things going wrong

cues.zh: 比如结构损坏、电力电子元件烧毁
cues.en: like structural failures, the power electronics frying itself

cues.zh: 所以经历过很多很多个“第一天”，但真正成功的那一天
cues.en: so there are many many first days, but the first day that it actually worked

cues.zh: 并不是持续飞行，当时大概只有 50% 的动力，算是有动力的滑翔。
cues.en: wasn't a sustained flight it was about 50% power, so it was a power glide.

cues.zh: 在那之前，我们都还没有百分之百的把握能做成。
cues.en: Until that occurred we still didn't know 100% whether this was really achievable.

cues.zh: 但自那之后我们就知道
cues.en: But after that point we knew that

cues.zh: 距离真正的成功飞行已经近在咫尺了。
cues.en: we were then within touching distance of successful flights.

cues.zh: 不久之后就迎来了首次持续飞行，那真的……
cues.en: And the first sustained flights followed quite soon after, which were...

cues.zh: 真的非常令人兴奋。
cues.en: which were pretty exciting.

cues.zh: 这很可能是重于空气的航空器首次实现纯固态飞行
cues.en: It's probably the first solid-state flight of a heavier-than-air vehicle

cues.zh: 我认为这很有潜力成为极具意义的一步。
cues.en: and I think that is, has the potential to be a step that is very interesting.

cues.zh: 当然，我们现在还不知道它是否
cues.en: Of course we don't yet know whether it will be

cues.zh: 具备实用价值并被广泛应用，我显然希望它能做到
cues.en: practically useful and widely used and obviously I hope it will be

cues.zh: 而且也抱有期待——它有很多潜在的应用场景。
cues.en: and have an expectation - there are a number of applications.

cues.zh: 确实存在一些限制，
cues.en: There are definitely some limits,

cues.zh: 其中一个限制是空气的击穿电压，
cues.en: so one of the limits is the breakdown voltage of air

cues.zh: 它会随着海拔变化。
cues.en: and that varies as a function of altitude.

cues.zh: 我们已经从理论上算出了
cues.en: And we've worked out theoretically what the

cues.zh: 推力密度的极限，也就是单位面积上
cues.en: limits are to the thrust density which is the amount of

cues.zh: 能够产生的推力。
cues.en: thrust force per unit area that's producible.

cues.zh: 这意味着在近期，
cues.en: Now what that suggests is that in the nearer term,

cues.zh: 制造更小的飞行器会更容易，比如无人机。
cues.en: it will be easier to create smaller vehicles like drones for example.

cues.zh: 我认为近期的优势可能在于降低噪声，
cues.en: I think the near-term advantage is probably in noise

cues.zh: 尤其是如果你想想，
cues.en: especially if you think that

cues.zh: 也许十年后，城市里到处都是无人机，
cues.en: perhaps in ten years we might have urban areas that are filled with drones doing

cues.zh: 执行监测交通、监测空气污染
cues.en: things like monitoring traffic, monitoring air pollution

cues.zh: 或许多我们还没想到的服务。
cues.en: or many other services we're yet to imagine.

cues.zh: 如今的无人机噪声很大，也很烦人。
cues.en: And drones today are quite noisy and irritating.

cues.zh: 我们肯定不希望城市环境被这些噪声污染，
cues.en: Now we wouldn't want our urban environments to be polluted by all this noise,

cues.zh: 所以，研发一种让无人机安静或几乎无声地飞行的推进方式，
cues.en: so developing a way of propelling drones that's silent or near silent would be

cues.zh: 在这种情况下会很有优势。
cues.en: advantageous in that context.

cues.zh: 在很多方面，现在的研发进展比过去容易多了。
cues.en: In many ways it's much easier to make progress now than it was in the past.

cues.zh: 你看我们身后的这架非凡的飞机，
cues.en: I mean if you look at this wonderful aircraft behind us

cues.zh: 它完成了人类史上首次跨大西洋飞行——大约在 1919 年。
cues.en: which was the first ever transatlantic flight - about 1919

cues.zh: 当时人们可是冒着生命危险在推动这种技术进步。
cues.en: I mean people were risking their lives to make that kind of progress.

cues.zh: 如今我们不用再拿生命冒险了，
cues.en: Today we're not risking our lives

cues.zh: 我们可以用遥控设备来做测试，
cues.en: we're able to test things using a remote control,

cues.zh: 测试机上完全不需要飞行员。
cues.en: without having to have pilots on board test vehicles.

cues.zh: 这意味着飞行器可以做得更小，
cues.en: That means the vehicles can be much smaller

cues.zh: 我们也就能用更少的资源来建造和测试它们。
cues.en: which enables us to build them and test them with less resources.

cues.zh: 至于未来的应用前景，
cues.en: In terms of how this fits in

cues.zh: 我不确定短期内能否看到载人的大型客机。
cues.en: I don't know whether you'll see large aircraft carrying people anytime soon.

cues.zh: 但如果真能实现，我显然会非常激动。
cues.en: But obviously I'd be very excited if that was the case.
